1: Project PartyRegistryServiceV1 {
2:   database_type: 'PostgreSQL'
3: 
4:   Note: '''
5:     Party Registry Service V1 - bounded context for tenant-scoped civil and legal identity.
6: 
7:     It is the system of record for identity data registered and maintained within
8:     each tenant. It owns Parties, their natural-person or legal-entity details,
9:     nationalities, official identifiers, and the database-managed identification
10:     scheme reference catalog used to normalize and validate those identifiers.
11: 
12:     It does not own customers, suppliers, employees, user accounts, authentication,
13:     authorization, operating organizations, addresses, contacts, subscriptions,
14:     audit storage, tax configuration, ownership structures, beneficial ownership,
15:     or legal/corporate relationship management.
16: 
17:     Other microservices keep party_id as an opaque reference and do not create
18:     foreign keys to this database.
19: 
20:     Country codes are logical references to the Geographic Reference Service,
21:     using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, without remote foreign keys.
22: 
23:     Complete identification values are encrypted with authenticated encryption.
24:     Exact lookup and permanent identifier uniqueness use a tenant-isolated
25:     HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint encoded as exactly 64 uppercase hexadecimal
26:     characters. Within one tenant and Identifier Scheme, the same normalized
27:     identifier value can never be registered more than once, regardless of
28:     lifecycle status.
29: 
30:     Identifier Schemes such as CEDULA, RUC and PASSPORT are database-managed
31:     reference data. Party Registry runtime reads them but does not create, update,
32:     delete or transition them through application use cases or REST endpoints.
33: 
34:     Keycloak authenticates accounts, but it is not the registry of persons.
35:     The relationship between an authenticated subject and party_id belongs to
36:     the Access Management Service.
37: 
38:     Every mutable business table contains created_at, created_by, updated_at and
39:     updated_by. Aggregate roots additionally contain version for optimistic
40:     concurrency control.
41: 
42:     party_outbox_events is infrastructure for reliable publication of tenant-scoped
43:     business events. It does not publish database-schema, Flyway, platform, or
44:     database-managed identifier-scheme catalog changes.
45:   '''
46: }
47: 
48: // Enums
49: 
50: Enum party_type {
51:   NATURAL_PERSON
52:   LEGAL_ENTITY
53: }
54: 
55: Enum party_record_status {
56:   DRAFT
57:   ACTIVE
58:   INACTIVE
59:   ARCHIVED
60: }
61: 
62: Enum identifier_category {
63:   NATIONAL_ID
64:   TAX_ID
65:   PASSPORT
66:   RESIDENCE_PERMIT
67:   LEGAL_REGISTRATION_NUMBER
68:   OTHER
69: }
70: 
71: Enum identifier_subject_type {
72:   NATURAL_PERSON
73:   LEGAL_ENTITY
74:   BOTH
75: }
76: 
77: Enum identifier_scheme_status {
78:   DRAFT
79:   ACTIVE
80:   DEPRECATED
81:   RETIRED
82: }
83: 
84: Enum party_identifier_status {
85:   PENDING_VERIFICATION
86:   VERIFIED
87:   REJECTED
88:   EXPIRED
89:   REVOKED
90: }
91: 
92: Enum party_outbox_aggregate_type {
93:   PARTY
94:   PARTY_IDENTIFIER
95: }
96: 
97: Enum outbox_status {
98:   PENDING
99:   PUBLISHED
100:   FAILED
101: }
102: 
103: // Tables
104: 
105: Table parties {
106:   id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`]
107:   tenant_id UUID [not null, note: 'Opaque reference to the tenant that owns this Party representation.']
108: 
109:   type party_type [not null]
110:   display_name VARCHAR(300) [not null, note: 'Canonical denormalized Party display name derived by Domain/Application from the corresponding detail row and persisted atomically.']
111:   record_status party_record_status [not null, default: 'DRAFT']
112: 
113:   created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
114:   created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Opaque authenticated subject or service principal.']
115:   updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
116:   updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Opaque authenticated subject or service principal.']
117:   version BIGINT [not null, default: 0, note: 'Optimistic concurrency version of the Party aggregate.']
118: 
119:   indexes {
120:     (tenant_id, id) [unique, name: 'uq_parties_tenant_id']
121:     (tenant_id, type, record_status) [name: 'ix_parties_tenant_type_status']
122:     (tenant_id, display_name) [name: 'ix_parties_tenant_display_name']
123:   }
124: 
125:   checks {
126:     `version >= 0` [name: 'ck_parties_nonnegative_version']
127:   }
128: 
129:   Note: '''
130:     Root of the Party aggregate. A Party is either NATURAL_PERSON or LEGAL_ENTITY.
131:     It is never a Customer, Supplier, Employee, User, Tenant, or operating company.
132: 
133:     display_name is derived deterministically by Domain/Application:
134:     - NATURAL_PERSON: normalize given_names and family_names independently, then
135:       join them with exactly one ASCII U+0020 SPACE.
136:     - LEGAL_ENTITY: normalize legal_name.
137: 
138:     Name normalization trims leading and trailing whitespace and collapses each
139:     internal run of whitespace to exactly one ASCII U+0020 SPACE. Letter case and
140:     diacritics are preserved. preferred_name and trade_name never replace the
141:     canonical display_name in V1. A mutation to a source name field and its
142:     resulting display_name update must commit atomically in the same transaction.
143: 
144:     Any mutation to natural_person_details, legal_entity_details or
145:     party_nationalities must increment parties.version in the same transaction.
146:   '''
147: }
148: 
149: Table natural_person_details {
150:   party_id UUID [pk, not null]
151: 
152:   given_names VARCHAR(200) [not null]
153:   family_names VARCHAR(200) [not null]
154:   preferred_name VARCHAR(200)
155:   birth_date DATE
156:   date_of_death DATE
157:   birth_country_code CHAR(2) [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.']
158: 
159:   created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
160:   created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
161:   updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
162:   updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
163: 
164:   checks {
165:     `date_of_death IS NULL OR birth_date IS NULL OR date_of_death >= birth_date` [name: 'ck_natural_person_life_dates']
166:     `birth_country_code IS NULL OR birth_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_natural_person_birth_country_code']
167:   }
168: 
169:   Note: '''
170:     One-to-one component of the Party aggregate for NATURAL_PERSON.
171: 
172:     Flyway must implement one deferred party/detail integrity mechanism using
173:     function fn_enforce_party_detail_type and these constraint-trigger objects:
174:     - ct_parties_detail_type on parties for INSERT and UPDATE of type.
175:     - ct_natural_person_details_party_type on natural_person_details for INSERT,
176:       UPDATE of party_id and DELETE.
177:     - ct_legal_entity_details_party_type on legal_entity_details for INSERT,
178:       UPDATE of party_id and DELETE.
179: 
180:     Each constraint trigger executes AFTER the stated row event, FOR EACH ROW,
181:     DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, so the invariant is evaluated at transaction
182:     commit after Party and detail rows may have been written in either order.
183: 
184:     At commit, each affected Party must satisfy exactly one detail invariant:
185:     - NATURAL_PERSON has exactly one natural_person_details row and zero
186:       legal_entity_details rows.
187:     - LEGAL_ENTITY has exactly one legal_entity_details row and zero
188:       natural_person_details rows.
189: 
190:     The Flyway migration and PostgreSQL integration tests must prove both valid
191:     insertion orderings in one transaction and must reject a missing required
192:     detail, a type-incompatible detail, both detail types for one Party, and any
193:     update/delete that would leave the committed invariant invalid.
194:   '''
195: }
196: 
197: Table legal_entity_details {
198:   party_id UUID [pk, not null]
199: 
200:   legal_name VARCHAR(300) [not null, note: 'Official registered name.']
201:   trade_name VARCHAR(300) [note: 'Primary trade name for V1; it does not replace legal_name.']
202:   legal_form_code VARCHAR(64) [note: 'Jurisdiction-qualified code, for example EC_SAS, EC_SA or US_LLC.']
203:   incorporation_country_code CHAR(2) [not null, note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.']
204:   incorporated_on DATE
205:   dissolved_on DATE
206: 
207:   created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
208:   created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
209:   updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
210:   updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]

338:   is_primary BOOLEAN [not null, default: false, note: 'Primary identifier within the same Party and identifier scheme.']
339:   status party_identifier_status [not null, default: 'PENDING_VERIFICATION']

341:   issued_on DATE
342:   expires_on DATE

369:     Aggregate for official identifiers such as national ID, RUC, passport,
370:     residence permit and legal registration number.
371: 
372:     normalized_value_hash is the canonical uppercase hexadecimal encoding of the
373:     HMAC-SHA-256 bytes. Lowercase hexadecimal, mixed case, prefixes and alternate
374:     textual encodings are invalid persisted representations.

376:     The tuple (tenant_id, identifier_scheme_id, normalized_value_hash) is a
377:     permanent business uniqueness key. Once a normalized identifier value has
378:     existed for a given tenant and Identifier Scheme, no second row may reuse
379:     that value, even when the previous row is REJECTED, EXPIRED or REVOKED.
380:     Lifecycle status never releases the identifier for reuse.

392:     permanent tenant+scheme+hash uniqueness rejects duplicate canonical hashes,
393:     the uppercase-hash check rejects lowercase/mixed/non-hex representations,
394:     and at most one VERIFIED primary identifier exists for the same
395:     tenant+Party+Identifier Scheme while non-primary or non-VERIFIED history is

397: 
398:     The application must ensure that the Party type is compatible with the
399:     identifier scheme applicable_subject_type.
400: 
401:     Public integration events must never contain the complete decrypted value.
402:   '''

Project PartyRegistryServiceV1 {
  database_type: 'PostgreSQL'

  Note: '''
    Party Registry Service V1 - bounded context for tenant-scoped civil and legal identity.

    It is the system of record for identity data registered and maintained within
    each tenant. It owns Parties, their natural-person or legal-entity details,
    nationalities, official identifiers, and the database-managed identification
    scheme reference catalog used to normalize and validate those identifiers.

    It does not own customers, suppliers, employees, user accounts, authentication,
    authorization, operating organizations, addresses, contacts, subscriptions,
    audit storage, tax configuration, ownership structures, beneficial ownership,
    or legal/corporate relationship management.

    Other microservices keep party_id as an opaque reference and do not create
    foreign keys to this database.

    Country codes are logical references to the Geographic Reference Service,
    using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, without remote foreign keys.

    Complete identification values are encrypted with authenticated encryption.
    Exact lookup and permanent identifier uniqueness use a tenant-isolated
    HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint encoded as exactly 64 uppercase hexadecimal
    characters. Within one tenant and Identifier Scheme, the same normalized
    identifier value can never be registered more than once, regardless of
    lifecycle status.

    Identifier Schemes such as CEDULA, RUC and PASSPORT are database-managed
    reference data. Party Registry runtime reads them but does not create, update,
    delete or transition them through application use cases or REST endpoints.

    Keycloak authenticates accounts, but it is not the registry of persons.
    The relationship between an authenticated subject and party_id belongs to
    the Access Management Service.

    Every mutable business table contains created_at, created_by, updated_at and
    updated_by. Aggregate roots additionally contain version for optimistic
    concurrency control.

    party_outbox_events is infrastructure for reliable publication of tenant-scoped
    business events. It does not publish database-schema, Flyway, platform, or
    database-managed identifier-scheme catalog changes.
  '''
}

// Enums

Enum party_type {
  NATURAL_PERSON
  LEGAL_ENTITY
}

Enum party_record_status {
  DRAFT
  ACTIVE
  INACTIVE
  ARCHIVED
}

Enum identifier_category {
  NATIONAL_ID
  TAX_ID
  PASSPORT
  RESIDENCE_PERMIT
  LEGAL_REGISTRATION_NUMBER
  OTHER
}

Enum identifier_subject_type {
  NATURAL_PERSON
  LEGAL_ENTITY
  BOTH
}

Enum identifier_scheme_status {
  DRAFT
  ACTIVE
  DEPRECATED
  RETIRED
}

Enum party_identifier_status {
  PENDING_VERIFICATION
  VERIFIED
  REJECTED
  EXPIRED
  REVOKED
}

Enum party_outbox_aggregate_type {
  PARTY
  PARTY_IDENTIFIER
}

Enum outbox_status {
  PENDING
  PUBLISHED
  FAILED
}

// Tables

Table parties {
  id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`]
  tenant_id UUID [not null, note: 'Opaque reference to the tenant that owns this Party representation.']

  type party_type [not null]
  display_name VARCHAR(300) [not null, note: 'Canonical denormalized Party display name derived by Domain/Application from the corresponding detail row and persisted atomically.']
  record_status party_record_status [not null, default: 'DRAFT']

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Opaque authenticated subject or service principal.']
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Opaque authenticated subject or service principal.']
  version BIGINT [not null, default: 0, note: 'Optimistic concurrency version of the Party aggregate.']

  indexes {
    (tenant_id, id) [unique, name: 'uq_parties_tenant_id']
    (tenant_id, type, record_status) [name: 'ix_parties_tenant_type_status']
    (tenant_id, display_name) [name: 'ix_parties_tenant_display_name']
  }

  checks {
    `version >= 0` [name: 'ck_parties_nonnegative_version']
  }

  Note: '''
    Root of the Party aggregate. A Party is either NATURAL_PERSON or LEGAL_ENTITY.
    It is never a Customer, Supplier, Employee, User, Tenant, or operating company.

    display_name is derived deterministically by Domain/Application:
    - NATURAL_PERSON: normalize given_names and family_names independently, then
      join them with exactly one ASCII U+0020 SPACE.
    - LEGAL_ENTITY: normalize legal_name.

    Name normalization trims leading and trailing whitespace and collapses each
    internal run of whitespace to exactly one ASCII U+0020 SPACE. Letter case and
    diacritics are preserved. preferred_name and trade_name never replace the
    canonical display_name in V1. A mutation to a source name field and its
    resulting display_name update must commit atomically in the same transaction.

    Any mutation to natural_person_details, legal_entity_details or
    party_nationalities must increment parties.version in the same transaction.
  '''
}

Table natural_person_details {
  party_id UUID [pk, not null]

  given_names VARCHAR(200) [not null]
  family_names VARCHAR(200) [not null]
  preferred_name VARCHAR(200)
  birth_date DATE
  date_of_death DATE
  birth_country_code CHAR(2) [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.']

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]

  checks {
    `date_of_death IS NULL OR birth_date IS NULL OR date_of_death >= birth_date` [name: 'ck_natural_person_life_dates']
    `birth_country_code IS NULL OR birth_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_natural_person_birth_country_code']
  }

  Note: '''
    One-to-one component of the Party aggregate for NATURAL_PERSON.

    Flyway must implement one deferred party/detail integrity mechanism using
    function fn_enforce_party_detail_type and these constraint-trigger objects:
    - ct_parties_detail_type on parties for INSERT and UPDATE of type.
    - ct_natural_person_details_party_type on natural_person_details for INSERT,
      UPDATE of party_id and DELETE.
    - ct_legal_entity_details_party_type on legal_entity_details for INSERT,
      UPDATE of party_id and DELETE.

    Each constraint trigger executes AFTER the stated row event, FOR EACH ROW,
    DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED, so the invariant is evaluated at transaction
    commit after Party and detail rows may have been written in either order.

    At commit, each affected Party must satisfy exactly one detail invariant:
    - NATURAL_PERSON has exactly one natural_person_details row and zero
      legal_entity_details rows.
    - LEGAL_ENTITY has exactly one legal_entity_details row and zero
      natural_person_details rows.

    The Flyway migration and PostgreSQL integration tests must prove both valid
    insertion orderings in one transaction and must reject a missing required
    detail, a type-incompatible detail, both detail types for one Party, and any
    update/delete that would leave the committed invariant invalid.
  '''
}

Table legal_entity_details {
  party_id UUID [pk, not null]

  legal_name VARCHAR(300) [not null, note: 'Official registered name.']
  trade_name VARCHAR(300) [note: 'Primary trade name for V1; it does not replace legal_name.']
  legal_form_code VARCHAR(64) [note: 'Jurisdiction-qualified code, for example EC_SAS, EC_SA or US_LLC.']
  incorporation_country_code CHAR(2) [not null, note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.']
  incorporated_on DATE
  dissolved_on DATE

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]

  checks {
    `dissolved_on IS NULL OR incorporated_on IS NULL OR dissolved_on >= incorporated_on` [name: 'ck_legal_entity_lifecycle_dates']
    `incorporation_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_legal_entity_incorporation_country_code']
  }

  Note: '''
    One-to-one component of the Party aggregate for LEGAL_ENTITY.
    It does not represent tenant configuration, tax configuration, ownership,
    corporate hierarchy, or commercial roles.
  '''
}

Table party_nationalities {
  id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`]
  party_id UUID [not null]

  country_code CHAR(2) [not null, note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.']
  is_primary BOOLEAN [not null, default: false]
  valid_from DATE
  valid_until DATE

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]

  indexes {
    (party_id, country_code) [name: 'ix_party_nationalities_country']
    (party_id, is_primary) [name: 'ix_party_nationalities_primary']
  }

  checks {
    `country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_party_nationality_country_code']
    `valid_until IS NULL OR valid_from IS NULL OR valid_until >= valid_from` [name: 'ck_party_nationality_validity']
  }

  Note: '''
    Nationalities known and maintained by the tenant for a natural-person Party.

    party_nationalities intentionally does not duplicate tenant_id. party_id
    references the globally unique parties.id, so the owning tenant is inherited
    unambiguously through that Party relationship.

    Flyway must create these exact partial unique indexes:
    - uq_party_nationalities_active_country on (party_id, country_code)
      WHERE valid_until IS NULL.
    - uq_party_nationalities_active_primary on (party_id)
      WHERE is_primary = true AND valid_until IS NULL.

    The Flyway migration and PostgreSQL integration tests must prove that a Party
    cannot have two active rows for the same country, cannot have two active
    primary nationalities, may retain ended historical rows, and may create a new
    active row after the previous matching nationality has been ended.
  '''
}

Table identifier_schemes {
  id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`]

  code VARCHAR(64) [not null, unique, note: 'Global stable code, for example EC_CEDULA, EC_RUC_NATURAL or US_EIN.']
  issuing_country_code CHAR(2) [not null, note: 'Logical ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 reference.']
  category identifier_category [not null]
  applicable_subject_type identifier_subject_type [not null]
  name VARCHAR(150) [not null]
  description VARCHAR(500)

  normalizer_key VARCHAR(64) [not null, note: 'Versioned implementation key, for example DIGITS_ONLY_V1.']
  validator_key VARCHAR(64) [not null, note: 'Versioned implementation key, for example ECUADOR_CEDULA_V1. It does not contain executable code.']
  minimum_length SMALLINT
  maximum_length SMALLINT
  requires_expiration BOOLEAN [not null, default: false]
  status identifier_scheme_status [not null, default: 'DRAFT']

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  version BIGINT [not null, default: 0]

  indexes {
    (issuing_country_code, category, applicable_subject_type, status) [name: 'ix_identifier_schemes_country_category']
  }

  checks {
    `issuing_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'` [name: 'ck_identifier_scheme_country_code']
    `minimum_length IS NULL OR minimum_length > 0` [name: 'ck_identifier_scheme_minimum_length']
    `maximum_length IS NULL OR maximum_length > 0` [name: 'ck_identifier_scheme_maximum_length']
    `minimum_length IS NULL OR maximum_length IS NULL OR maximum_length >= minimum_length` [name: 'ck_identifier_scheme_length_range']
    `version >= 0` [name: 'ck_identifier_schemes_nonnegative_version']
  }

  Note: '''
    Global database-managed reference catalog used internally by Party Registry
    to normalize and validate official Party identifiers, for example CEDULA,
    RUC and PASSPORT schemes.

    Party Registry runtime treats this table as read-only. The runtime database
    role must not INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE identifier_schemes rows. Scheme rows
    are introduced or changed only through the governed database migration and/or
    explicitly authorized database-administration path using separate credentials.

    Persisted status, audit and version fields describe database-managed catalog
    state; they do not imply a Party Registry REST lifecycle or Scheme
    Administration application capability.

    Database-managed Scheme changes are not published through the tenant Party
    outbox. Persisted normalizer/validator keys must remain compatible with the
    deployed Party Registry implementation catalog; the runtime fails closed on
    unusable required configuration rather than rewriting this table.
  '''
}

Table party_identifiers {
  id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`]
  tenant_id UUID [not null]
  party_id UUID [not null]
  identifier_scheme_id UUID [not null]

  issuer_code VARCHAR(64) [note: 'Issuing authority, for example SRI or REGISTRO_CIVIL.']

  encrypted_value TEXT [not null, note: 'Authenticated encryption; never plain text.']
  encryption_key_version SMALLINT [not null, note: 'Version of the runtime-injected encryption key used for this ciphertext.']
  normalized_value_hash CHAR(64) [not null, note: 'Tenant-isolated HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint encoded as exactly 64 uppercase hexadecimal characters; used for exact lookup and permanent uniqueness within the tenant and Identifier Scheme.']
  masked_value VARCHAR(64) [not null, note: 'Safe representation for UI and logs.']
  normalization_version SMALLINT [not null, default: 1]

  is_primary BOOLEAN [not null, default: false, note: 'Primary identifier within the same Party and identifier scheme.']
  status party_identifier_status [not null, default: 'PENDING_VERIFICATION']

  issued_on DATE
  expires_on DATE
  verified_at TIMESTAMPTZ
  verified_by VARCHAR(128)

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null]
  version BIGINT [not null, default: 0, note: 'Optimistic concurrency version of the Party Identifier aggregate.']

  indexes {
    (tenant_id, identifier_scheme_id, normalized_value_hash) [unique, name: 'uq_party_identifier_tenant_scheme_hash']
    (tenant_id, party_id, identifier_scheme_id, status) [name: 'ix_party_identifiers_party_scheme_status']
    (tenant_id, party_id, is_primary) [name: 'ix_party_identifiers_primary']
  }

  checks {
    `expires_on IS NULL OR issued_on IS NULL OR expires_on >= issued_on` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_validity_dates']
    `(status = 'VERIFIED' AND verified_at IS NOT NULL AND verified_by IS NOT NULL) OR status <> 'VERIFIED'` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_verification']
    `(status = 'EXPIRED' AND expires_on IS NOT NULL) OR status <> 'EXPIRED'` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_expired_date']
    `normalized_value_hash ~ '^[0-9A-F]{64}$'` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_hash_upper_hex']
    `normalization_version > 0` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_normalization_version']
    `encryption_key_version > 0` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_encryption_key_version']
    `version >= 0` [name: 'ck_party_identifier_nonnegative_version']
  }

  Note: '''
    Aggregate for official identifiers such as national ID, RUC, passport,
    residence permit and legal registration number.

    normalized_value_hash is the canonical uppercase hexadecimal encoding of the
    HMAC-SHA-256 bytes. Lowercase hexadecimal, mixed case, prefixes and alternate
    textual encodings are invalid persisted representations.

    The tuple (tenant_id, identifier_scheme_id, normalized_value_hash) is a
    permanent business uniqueness key. Once a normalized identifier value has
    existed for a given tenant and Identifier Scheme, no second row may reuse
    that value, even when the previous row is REJECTED, EXPIRED or REVOKED.
    Lifecycle status never releases the identifier for reuse.

    The same normalized identifier value may exist in another tenant or under a
    different Identifier Scheme because either change produces a different
    uniqueness scope.

    Flyway must create the partial unique index
      uq_party_identifiers_verified_primary_scheme
    on (tenant_id, party_id, identifier_scheme_id)
    WHERE is_primary = true AND status = 'VERIFIED'.

    The Flyway migration and PostgreSQL integration tests must prove that the
    permanent tenant+scheme+hash uniqueness rejects duplicate canonical hashes,
    the uppercase-hash check rejects lowercase/mixed/non-hex representations,
    and at most one VERIFIED primary identifier exists for the same
    tenant+Party+Identifier Scheme while non-primary or non-VERIFIED history is
    retained.

    The application must ensure that the Party type is compatible with the
    identifier scheme applicable_subject_type.

    Public integration events must never contain the complete decrypted value.
  '''
}

Table party_outbox_events {
  id UUID [pk, not null, default: `uuidv7()`, note: 'Integration event identifier.']
  tenant_id UUID [not null]

  aggregate_type party_outbox_aggregate_type [not null]
  aggregate_id UUID [not null]
  aggregate_version BIGINT [not null]

  event_type VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Versioned business contract, for example party.created.v1 or party.identifier-verified.v1.']
  event_schema_version SMALLINT [not null, default: 1]
  payload JSONB [not null, note: 'Minimal integration payload without full identifiers or unnecessary personal data.']

  occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  correlation_id VARCHAR(128)
  causation_id VARCHAR(128)

  status outbox_status [not null, default: 'PENDING']
  publish_attempts INTEGER [not null, default: 0]
  next_attempt_at TIMESTAMPTZ
  last_attempt_at TIMESTAMPTZ
  published_at TIMESTAMPTZ
  last_error_code VARCHAR(64)
  last_error_detail VARCHAR(1000)

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  created_by VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Service principal that created the business event.']
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ [not null, default: `now()`]
  updated_by VARCHAR(128) [not null, note: 'Publisher instance or service principal that last changed delivery state.']
  version BIGINT [not null, default: 0, note: 'Optimistic concurrency version for delivery-state transitions.']

  indexes {
    (status, next_attempt_at, created_at) [name: 'ix_party_outbox_delivery']
    (tenant_id, aggregate_type, aggregate_id, aggregate_version) [name: 'ix_party_outbox_aggregate']
    correlation_id [name: 'ix_party_outbox_correlation']
  }

  checks {
    `aggregate_version >= 0` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_nonnegative_aggregate_version']
    `event_schema_version > 0` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_positive_schema_version']
    `publish_attempts >= 0` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_nonnegative_attempts']
    `version >= 0` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_nonnegative_version']
    `(status = 'PUBLISHED' AND published_at IS NOT NULL) OR (status <> 'PUBLISHED' AND published_at IS NULL)` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_published_at']
    `(status = 'FAILED' AND last_error_code IS NOT NULL) OR status <> 'FAILED'` [name: 'ck_party_outbox_failed_error']
  }

  Note: '''
    Transactional Outbox for tenant-scoped Party Registry business events.

    The business mutation and outbox insertion must be committed in the same
    PostgreSQL transaction. A separate publisher processes PENDING rows using
    SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

    Aggregate mapping:
    - PARTY: aggregate_id = parties.id and aggregate_version = parties.version.
      This includes changes to natural_person_details, legal_entity_details and
      party_nationalities; parties.version must be incremented in the same transaction.
    - PARTY_IDENTIFIER: aggregate_id = party_identifiers.id and
      aggregate_version = party_identifiers.version.

    The table does not publish:
    - PostgreSQL schema changes.
    - Flyway migrations.
    - Platform or infrastructure events.
    - database-managed identifier_schemes catalog changes.

    Delivery is at-least-once. Consumers must be idempotent using id as event_id.
  '''
}

Future corrections may not edit either migration.
60: 
61: ### Representative integrity cases
62: 
63: - Commit valid natural/legal Parties with detail-before-Party and Party-before-detail ordering; reject missing, wrong, dual, moved, deleted, or type-updated detail states at deferred-constraint evaluation.
64: - Reject invalid life dates and country-code syntax.
65: - Reject duplicate active nationality country and active primary rows; retain ended history and permit a replacement active row after ending the prior row.
66: - Reject cross-tenant Party Identifier references through the composite FK.
67: - Reject lowercase, mixed-case, non-hex, prefixed or non-64-character hashes.
68: - Reject duplicate tenant+Scheme+hash values in every identifier status; permit the same hash in another tenant or Scheme; verify concurrent duplicates allow at most one commit.
69: - Reject a second verified primary identifier for one tenant+Party+Scheme while permitting non-primary and non-VERIFIED history.
70: - Exercise every positive/nonnegative, date, verification, expiration, published-state and failed-state check.
71: - Verify runtime reads Schemes and is denied Scheme `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`; verify runtime has no physical `DELETE` on any table and no direct function execution.
72: - Verify migration-owner catalog changes create no outbox event automatically.
73: 
74: ### Failure, atomicity and recovery
75: 
76: - Execute V1 transactionally in an isolated database with a controlled precondition failure (missing runtime role) and prove no V1 schema object or successful Flyway history row remains. Recreate the required role and rerun the complete chain successfully. Separately force a V2 execution failure in a disposable V1-only database and prove its two `ALTER CONSTRAINT` statements roll back atomically; do not use `clean`, `repair`, `baseline`, checksum edits, or reverse SQL.
77: - A production failure stops application rollout. Recovery is correction of the external precondition or migration defect followed by forward execution. V1 is not edited; V2 is the immutable roll-forward correction. Any later defect requires the next immutable migration.
78: 
79: ## Lock, duration and operational analysis
80: 
81: - Risk classification: `LOW` for V1's initial additive empty schema and `MEDIUM` for V2 because altering foreign-key timing acquires table locks on an existing V1 schema; operational rollout is therefore `MEDIUM`.
82: - V1 creates new types, empty tables, constraints and indexes only. V2 changes only foreign-key catalog attributes: it scans or backfills no rows, does not recreate or revalidate the foreign keys, rewrites no table, and generates no row-transformation WAL.
83: - V1 takes catalog locks for the transaction and exclusive locks only on newly created objects. V2 requires `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` locks on `natural_person_details` and `legal_entity_details` for two short metadata-only statements; apply before enabling application traffic or in an approved bounded window if a V1 environment already accepts traffic. No index uses `CONCURRENTLY` because V1 builds each index on a new empty table.
84: - Pre-deployment must validate PostgreSQL major version 18, immutable V1 checksum and Flyway order, the actual starting version (V0 or V1), existence and separation of `party_registry_runtime` from the migration login, backup/restore readiness, absence of long transactions that could delay V2 locks, and compatible application deployment order.
85: - Completion signals are successful Flyway history through V2, both detail foreign keys reporting `condeferrable=true` and `condeferred=true`, zero invalid indexes/constraints, complete schema-fidelity query results, runtime Scheme write denials, and application readiness. Stop on any unexpected pre-existing object, checksum mismatch, role mismatch, lock timeout, partial state, or integrity failure.
86: - Database reversal is not an approved rollback. Before application data is accepted, correct failures and roll forward. After data exists, retain V1/V2 and repair through a new immutable migration; application rollback/re-promotion must remain schema-compatible and operations-owned.

### Supported prior schema and data preservation

The initial supported-prior-schema case is an empty database at V0. Clean-chain evidence must migrate V0 through V1 and V2 once and prove a second run is a no-op. Because committed V1 is now an immutable supported intermediate schema, upgrade evidence must also create a V1-only database, insert representative valid Party/detail data in the ordering V1 permits, apply V2 exactly once, prove rows are unchanged, prove both detail foreign keys are deferred in `pg_constraint`, and prove a second run is a no-op. Future corrections may not edit either migration.

### Representative integrity cases

- Commit valid natural/legal Parties with detail-before-Party and Party-before-detail ordering; reject missing, wrong, dual, moved, deleted, or type-updated detail states at deferred-constraint evaluation.
- Reject invalid life dates and country-code syntax.
- Reject duplicate active nationality country and active primary rows; retain ended history and permit a replacement active row after ending the prior row.
- Reject cross-tenant Party Identifier references through the composite FK.
- Reject lowercase, mixed-case, non-hex, prefixed or non-64-character hashes.
- Reject duplicate tenant+Scheme+hash values in every identifier status; permit the same hash in another tenant or Scheme; verify concurrent duplicates allow at most one commit.
- Reject a second verified primary identifier for one tenant+Party+Scheme while permitting non-primary and non-VERIFIED history.
- Exercise every positive/nonnegative, date, verification, expiration, published-state and failed-state check.
- Verify runtime reads Schemes and is denied Scheme `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`; verify runtime has no physical `DELETE` on any table and no direct function execution.
- Verify migration-owner catalog changes create no outbox event automatically.

### Failure, atomicity and recovery

- Execute V1 transactionally in an isolated database with a controlled precondition failure (missing runtime role) and prove no V1 schema object or successful Flyway history row remains. Recreate the required role and rerun the complete chain successfully. Separately force a V2 execution failure in a disposable V1-only database and prove its two `ALTER CONSTRAINT` statements roll back atomically; do not use `clean`, `repair`, `baseline`, checksum edits, or reverse SQL.
- A production failure stops application rollout. Recovery is correction of the external precondition or migration defect followed by forward execution. V1 is not edited; V2 is the immutable roll-forward correction. Any later defect requires the next immutable migration.

## Lock, duration and operational analysis

- Risk classification: `LOW` for V1's initial additive empty schema and `MEDIUM` for V2 because altering foreign-key timing acquires table locks on an existing V1 schema; operational rollout is therefore `MEDIUM`.
- V1 creates new types, empty tables, constraints and indexes only. V2 changes only foreign-key catalog attributes: it scans or backfills no rows, does not recreate or revalidate the foreign keys, rewrites no table, and generates no row-transformation WAL.
- V1 takes catalog locks for the transaction and exclusive locks only on newly created objects. V2 requires `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` locks on `natural_person_details` and `legal_entity_details` for two short metadata-only statements; apply before enabling application traffic or in an approved bounded window if a V1 environment already accepts traffic. No index uses `CONCURRENTLY` because V1 builds each index on a new empty table.
- Pre-deployment must validate PostgreSQL major version 18, immutable V1 checksum and Flyway order, the actual starting version (V0 or V1), existence and separation of `party_registry_runtime` from the migration login, backup/restore readiness, absence of long transactions that could delay V2 locks, and compatible application deployment order.
- Completion signals are successful Flyway history through V2, both detail foreign keys reporting `condeferrable=true` and `condeferred=true`, zero invalid indexes/constraints, complete schema-fidelity query results, runtime Scheme write denials, and application readiness. Stop on any unexpected pre-existing object, checksum mismatch, role mismatch, lock timeout, partial state, or integrity failure.
- Database reversal is not an approved rollback. Before application data is accepted, correct failures and roll forward. After data exists, retain V1/V2 and repair through a new immutable migration; application rollback/re-promotion must remain schema-compatible and operations-owned.

291:     'Official Party identifiers. Complete values are authenticated-encrypted; exact lookup and permanent tenant-and-scheme uniqueness use the uppercase tenant-isolated HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint.';
292: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.issuer_code IS
293:     'Issuing authority, for example SRI or REGISTRO_CIVIL.';
294: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.encrypted_value IS
295:     'Authenticated encryption; never plain text.';
296: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.encryption_key_version IS
297:     'Version of the runtime-injected encryption key used for this ciphertext.';
298: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.normalized_value_hash IS
299:     'Tenant-isolated HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint encoded as exactly 64 uppercase hexadecimal characters; used for exact lookup and permanent uniqueness within the tenant and Identifier Scheme.';
300: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.masked_value IS
301:     'Safe representation for UI and logs.';
302: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.is_primary IS
303:     'Primary identifier within the same Party and Identifier Scheme.';
304: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.version IS
305:     'Optimistic concurrency version of the Party Identifier aggregate.';
306: 
307: CREATE TABLE public.party_outbox_events (
308:     id uuid DEFAULT uuidv7() NOT NULL,
309:     tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
310:     aggregate_type public.party_outbox_aggregate_type NOT NULL,
311:     aggregate_id uuid NOT NULL,
312:     aggregate_version bigint NOT NULL,
313:     event_type varchar(128) NOT NULL,
314:     event_schema_version smallint DEFAULT 1 NOT NULL,
315:     payload jsonb NOT NULL,
316:     occurred_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
317:     correlation_id varchar(128),
318:     causation_id varchar(128),
319:     status public.outbox_status DEFAULT 'PENDING' NOT NULL,
320:     publish_attempts integer DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL,
321:     next_attempt_at timestamptz,
322:     last_attempt_at timestamptz,
323:     published_at timestamptz,
324:     last_error_code varchar(64),
325:     last_error_detail varchar(1000),
326:     created_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
327:     created_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
328:     updated_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
329:     updated_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
330:     version bigint DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL,
331:     CONSTRAINT pk_party_outbox_events PRIMARY KEY (id),
332:     CONSTRAINT ck_party_outbox_nonnegative_aggregate_version CHECK (aggregate_version >= 0),
333:     CONSTRAINT ck_party_outbox_positive_schema_version CHECK (event_schema_version > 0),
334:     CONSTRAINT ck_party_outbox_nonnegative_attempts CHECK (publish_attempts >= 0),
335:     CONSTRAINT ck_party_outbox_nonnegative_version CHECK (version >= 0),
336:     CONSTRAINT ck_party_outbox_published_at
337:         CHECK ((status = 'PUBLISHED' AND published_at IS NOT NULL)
338:                OR (status <> 'PUBLISHED' AND published_at IS NULL)),
339:     CONSTRAINT ck_party_outbox_failed_error
340:         CHECK ((status = 'FAILED' AND last_error_code IS NOT NULL) OR status <> 'FAILED')
341: );
342: 
343: CREATE INDEX ix_party_outbox_delivery
344:     ON public.party_outbox_events (status, next_attempt_at, created_at);
345: CREATE INDEX ix_party_outbox_aggregate
346:     ON public.party_outbox_events
347:     (tenant_id, aggregate_type, aggregate_id, aggregate_version);
348: CREATE INDEX ix_party_outbox_correlation
349:     ON public.party_outbox_events (correlation_id);
350: 
351: COMMENT ON TABLE public.party_outbox_events IS
352:     'Transactional Outbox for tenant-scoped Party and Party Identifier events. Business mutation and event insertion commit together; a separate publisher uses bounded SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claims and at-least-once delivery.';
353: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_outbox_events.id IS
354:     'Integration event identifier.';
355: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_outbox_events.event_type IS
356:     'Versioned business contract, for example party.created.v1 or party.identifier-verified.v1.';
357: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_outbox_events.payload IS
358:     'Minimal integration payload without full identifiers or unnecessary personal data.';
359: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_outbox_events.created_by IS
360:     'Service principal that created the business event.';
361: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_outbox_events.updated_by IS
362:     'Publisher instance or service principal that last changed delivery state.';
363: COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_outbox_events.version IS
364:     'Optimistic concurrency version for delivery-state transitions.';
365: 
366: CREATE FUNCTION public.fn_enforce_party_detail_type()
367: RETURNS trigger
368: LANGUAGE plpgsql
369: AS $function$
370: DECLARE
371:     affected_party_id uuid;
372:     affected_party_ids uuid[];
373:     party_kind public.party_type;
374:     natural_detail_count integer;
375:     legal_detail_count integer;
376: BEGIN
377:     IF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'parties' THEN
378:         affected_party_ids := ARRAY[NEW.id];
379:     ELSIF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
380:         affected_party_ids := ARRAY[OLD.party_id];
381:     ELSIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.party_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.party_id THEN
382:         affected_party_ids := ARRAY[OLD.party_id, NEW.party_id];
383:     ELSE
384:         affected_party_ids := ARRAY[NEW.party_id];
385:     END IF;
386: 
387:     FOREACH affected_party_id IN ARRAY affected_party_ids
388:     LOOP
389:         SELECT p.type
390:           INTO party_kind
391:           FROM public.parties AS p
392:          WHERE p.id = affected_party_id;
393: 
394:         IF NOT FOUND THEN
395:             CONTINUE;
396:         END IF;
397: 
398:         SELECT count(*)
399:           INTO natural_detail_count
400:           FROM public.natural_person_details AS npd
401:          WHERE npd.party_id = affected_party_id;
402: 
403:         SELECT count(*)
404:           INTO legal_detail_count
405:           FROM public.legal_entity_details AS led
406:          WHERE led.party_id = affected_party_id;
407: 
408:         IF (party_kind = 'NATURAL_PERSON'
409:             AND (natural_detail_count <> 1 OR legal_detail_count <> 0))
410:            OR (party_kind = 'LEGAL_ENTITY'
411:                AND (natural_detail_count <> 0 OR legal_detail_count <> 1)) THEN
412:             RAISE EXCEPTION USING
413:                 ERRCODE = 'integrity_constraint_violation',
414:                 MESSAGE = 'party detail type invariant violated',
415:                 DETAIL = format('party_id=%s', affected_party_id),
416:                 CONSTRAINT = 'ct_parties_detail_type';
417:         END IF;
418:     END LOOP;
419: 
420:     RETURN NULL;
421: END;
422: $function$;
423: 
424: COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.fn_enforce_party_detail_type() IS
425:     'Deferred commit-time enforcement that every Party has exactly one detail row matching its immutable Party type.';
426: 
427: CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ct_parties_detail_type
428: AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF type ON public.parties
429: DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
430: FOR EACH ROW
431: EXECUTE FUNCTION public.fn_enforce_party_detail_type();
432: 
433: CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ct_natural_person_details_party_type
434: AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF party_id OR DELETE ON public.natural_person_details
435: DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
436: FOR EACH ROW
437: EXECUTE FUNCTION public.fn_enforce_party_detail_type();
438: 
439: CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ct_legal_entity_details_party_type
440: AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF party_id OR DELETE ON public.legal_entity_details
441: DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
442: FOR EACH ROW
443: EXECUTE FUNCTION public.fn_enforce_party_detail_type();
444: 
445: -- PUBLIC receives no object access. PostgreSQL grants EXECUTE on new functions
446: -- to PUBLIC by default, so remove that implicit grant explicitly.
447: REVOKE ALL ON TABLE
448:     public.parties,
449:     public.natural_person_details,
450:     public.legal_entity_details,
451:     public.party_nationalities,
452:     public.identifier_schemes,
453:     public.party_identifiers,
454:     public.party_outbox_events
455: FROM PUBLIC;
456: REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.fn_enforce_party_detail_type() FROM PUBLIC;
457: 
458: -- The runtime can perform only logical lifecycle changes; no table DELETE is
459: -- granted. Identifier Schemes are query-only for the runtime by Amendment 002.
460: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON TABLE
461:     public.parties,
462:     public.natural_person_details,
463:     public.legal_entity_details,
464:     public.party_nationalities,
465:     public.party_identifiers,
466:     public.party_outbox_events
467: TO party_registry_runtime;
468: GRANT SELECT ON TABLE public.identifier_schemes TO party_registry_runtime;

-- T010 / docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml: initial Party Registry V1 schema.
-- PostgreSQL 18 supplies uuidv7() in core; no extension is required.
-- Precondition: the separately provisioned NOLOGIN/group role
-- party_registry_runtime exists. The Flyway connection role owns all objects.

CREATE TYPE public.party_type AS ENUM (
    'NATURAL_PERSON',
    'LEGAL_ENTITY'
);

CREATE TYPE public.party_record_status AS ENUM (
    'DRAFT',
    'ACTIVE',
    'INACTIVE',
    'ARCHIVED'
);

CREATE TYPE public.identifier_category AS ENUM (
    'NATIONAL_ID',
    'TAX_ID',
    'PASSPORT',
    'RESIDENCE_PERMIT',
    'LEGAL_REGISTRATION_NUMBER',
    'OTHER'
);

CREATE TYPE public.identifier_subject_type AS ENUM (
    'NATURAL_PERSON',
    'LEGAL_ENTITY',
    'BOTH'
);

CREATE TYPE public.identifier_scheme_status AS ENUM (
    'DRAFT',
    'ACTIVE',
    'DEPRECATED',
    'RETIRED'
);

CREATE TYPE public.party_identifier_status AS ENUM (
    'PENDING_VERIFICATION',
    'VERIFIED',
    'REJECTED',
    'EXPIRED',
    'REVOKED'
);

CREATE TYPE public.party_outbox_aggregate_type AS ENUM (
    'PARTY',
    'PARTY_IDENTIFIER'
);

CREATE TYPE public.outbox_status AS ENUM (
    'PENDING',
    'PUBLISHED',
    'FAILED'
);

CREATE TABLE public.parties (
    id uuid DEFAULT uuidv7() NOT NULL,
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    type public.party_type NOT NULL,
    display_name varchar(300) NOT NULL,
    record_status public.party_record_status DEFAULT 'DRAFT' NOT NULL,
    created_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    created_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    updated_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    updated_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    version bigint DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_parties PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT uq_parties_tenant_id UNIQUE (tenant_id, id),
    CONSTRAINT ck_parties_nonnegative_version CHECK (version >= 0)
);

CREATE INDEX ix_parties_tenant_type_status
    ON public.parties (tenant_id, type, record_status);
CREATE INDEX ix_parties_tenant_display_name
    ON public.parties (tenant_id, display_name);

COMMENT ON TABLE public.parties IS
    'Root of the Party aggregate. A Party is either NATURAL_PERSON or LEGAL_ENTITY. display_name is derived deterministically by Domain/Application from its matching detail row; detail or nationality mutations increment parties.version in the same transaction.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.parties.tenant_id IS
    'Opaque reference to the tenant that owns this Party representation.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.parties.display_name IS
    'Canonical denormalized Party display name derived by Domain/Application from the corresponding detail row and persisted atomically.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.parties.created_by IS
    'Opaque authenticated subject or service principal.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.parties.updated_by IS
    'Opaque authenticated subject or service principal.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.parties.version IS
    'Optimistic concurrency version of the Party aggregate.';

CREATE TABLE public.natural_person_details (
    party_id uuid NOT NULL,
    given_names varchar(200) NOT NULL,
    family_names varchar(200) NOT NULL,
    preferred_name varchar(200),
    birth_date date,
    date_of_death date,
    birth_country_code char(2),
    created_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    created_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    updated_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    updated_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_natural_person_details PRIMARY KEY (party_id),
    CONSTRAINT ck_natural_person_life_dates
        CHECK (date_of_death IS NULL OR birth_date IS NULL OR date_of_death >= birth_date),
    CONSTRAINT ck_natural_person_birth_country_code
        CHECK (birth_country_code IS NULL OR birth_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'),
    CONSTRAINT fk_natural_person_details_party
        FOREIGN KEY (party_id) REFERENCES public.parties (id)
        ON UPDATE NO ACTION ON DELETE RESTRICT
);

COMMENT ON TABLE public.natural_person_details IS
    'One-to-one component of the Party aggregate for NATURAL_PERSON. Commit-time type/detail integrity is enforced by fn_enforce_party_detail_type and deferred constraint triggers.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.natural_person_details.birth_country_code IS
    'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.';

CREATE TABLE public.legal_entity_details (
    party_id uuid NOT NULL,
    legal_name varchar(300) NOT NULL,
    trade_name varchar(300),
    legal_form_code varchar(64),
    incorporation_country_code char(2) NOT NULL,
    incorporated_on date,
    dissolved_on date,
    created_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    created_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    updated_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    updated_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_legal_entity_details PRIMARY KEY (party_id),
    CONSTRAINT ck_legal_entity_lifecycle_dates
        CHECK (dissolved_on IS NULL OR incorporated_on IS NULL OR dissolved_on >= incorporated_on),
    CONSTRAINT ck_legal_entity_incorporation_country_code
        CHECK (incorporation_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'),
    CONSTRAINT fk_legal_entity_details_party
        FOREIGN KEY (party_id) REFERENCES public.parties (id)
        ON UPDATE NO ACTION ON DELETE RESTRICT
);

COMMENT ON TABLE public.legal_entity_details IS
    'One-to-one component of the Party aggregate for LEGAL_ENTITY. It does not represent tenant configuration, tax configuration, ownership, corporate hierarchy, or commercial roles.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.legal_entity_details.legal_name IS
    'Official registered name.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.legal_entity_details.trade_name IS
    'Primary trade name for V1; it does not replace legal_name.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.legal_entity_details.legal_form_code IS
    'Jurisdiction-qualified code, for example EC_SAS, EC_SA or US_LLC.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.legal_entity_details.incorporation_country_code IS
    'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.';

CREATE TABLE public.party_nationalities (
    id uuid DEFAULT uuidv7() NOT NULL,
    party_id uuid NOT NULL,
    country_code char(2) NOT NULL,
    is_primary boolean DEFAULT false NOT NULL,
    valid_from date,
    valid_until date,
    created_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    created_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    updated_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    updated_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_party_nationalities PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_nationality_country_code
        CHECK (country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_nationality_validity
        CHECK (valid_until IS NULL OR valid_from IS NULL OR valid_until >= valid_from),
    CONSTRAINT fk_party_nationalities_party
        FOREIGN KEY (party_id) REFERENCES public.parties (id)
        ON UPDATE NO ACTION ON DELETE RESTRICT
);

CREATE INDEX ix_party_nationalities_country
    ON public.party_nationalities (party_id, country_code);
CREATE INDEX ix_party_nationalities_primary
    ON public.party_nationalities (party_id, is_primary);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_party_nationalities_active_country
    ON public.party_nationalities (party_id, country_code)
    WHERE valid_until IS NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_party_nationalities_active_primary
    ON public.party_nationalities (party_id)
    WHERE is_primary = true AND valid_until IS NULL;

COMMENT ON TABLE public.party_nationalities IS
    'Nationalities known and maintained by the tenant for a natural-person Party. Tenant ownership is inherited through the globally unique party_id; active rows have valid_until IS NULL.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_nationalities.country_code IS
    'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.';

CREATE TABLE public.identifier_schemes (
    id uuid DEFAULT uuidv7() NOT NULL,
    code varchar(64) NOT NULL,
    issuing_country_code char(2) NOT NULL,
    category public.identifier_category NOT NULL,
    applicable_subject_type public.identifier_subject_type NOT NULL,
    name varchar(150) NOT NULL,
    description varchar(500),
    normalizer_key varchar(64) NOT NULL,
    validator_key varchar(64) NOT NULL,
    minimum_length smallint,
    maximum_length smallint,
    requires_expiration boolean DEFAULT false NOT NULL,
    status public.identifier_scheme_status DEFAULT 'DRAFT' NOT NULL,
    created_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    created_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    updated_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    updated_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    version bigint DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_identifier_schemes PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT uq_identifier_schemes_code UNIQUE (code),
    CONSTRAINT ck_identifier_scheme_country_code
        CHECK (issuing_country_code ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'),
    CONSTRAINT ck_identifier_scheme_minimum_length
        CHECK (minimum_length IS NULL OR minimum_length > 0),
    CONSTRAINT ck_identifier_scheme_maximum_length
        CHECK (maximum_length IS NULL OR maximum_length > 0),
    CONSTRAINT ck_identifier_scheme_length_range
        CHECK (minimum_length IS NULL OR maximum_length IS NULL OR maximum_length >= minimum_length),
    CONSTRAINT ck_identifier_schemes_nonnegative_version CHECK (version >= 0)
);

CREATE INDEX ix_identifier_schemes_country_category
    ON public.identifier_schemes
    (issuing_country_code, category, applicable_subject_type, status);

COMMENT ON TABLE public.identifier_schemes IS
    'Global database-managed Identifier Scheme reference catalog. Party Registry runtime reads this table but cannot insert, update, or delete rows; governed database credentials manage catalog changes.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.identifier_schemes.code IS
    'Global stable code, for example EC_CEDULA, EC_RUC_NATURAL or US_EIN.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.identifier_schemes.issuing_country_code IS
    'Logical ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 reference.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.identifier_schemes.normalizer_key IS
    'Versioned implementation key, for example DIGITS_ONLY_V1.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.identifier_schemes.validator_key IS
    'Versioned implementation key, for example ECUADOR_CEDULA_V1. It does not contain executable code.';

CREATE TABLE public.party_identifiers (
    id uuid DEFAULT uuidv7() NOT NULL,
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    party_id uuid NOT NULL,
    identifier_scheme_id uuid NOT NULL,
    issuer_code varchar(64),
    encrypted_value text NOT NULL,
    encryption_key_version smallint NOT NULL,
    normalized_value_hash char(64) NOT NULL,
    masked_value varchar(64) NOT NULL,
    normalization_version smallint DEFAULT 1 NOT NULL,
    is_primary boolean DEFAULT false NOT NULL,
    status public.party_identifier_status DEFAULT 'PENDING_VERIFICATION' NOT NULL,
    issued_on date,
    expires_on date,
    verified_at timestamptz,
    verified_by varchar(128),
    created_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    created_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    updated_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    updated_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    version bigint DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_party_identifiers PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT uq_party_identifier_tenant_scheme_hash
        UNIQUE (tenant_id, identifier_scheme_id, normalized_value_hash),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_identifier_validity_dates
        CHECK (expires_on IS NULL OR issued_on IS NULL OR expires_on >= issued_on),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_identifier_verification
        CHECK ((status = 'VERIFIED' AND verified_at IS NOT NULL AND verified_by IS NOT NULL)
               OR status <> 'VERIFIED'),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_identifier_expired_date
        CHECK ((status = 'EXPIRED' AND expires_on IS NOT NULL) OR status <> 'EXPIRED'),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_identifier_hash_upper_hex
        CHECK (normalized_value_hash ~ '^[0-9A-F]{64}$'),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_identifier_normalization_version CHECK (normalization_version > 0),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_identifier_encryption_key_version CHECK (encryption_key_version > 0),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_identifier_nonnegative_version CHECK (version >= 0),
    CONSTRAINT fk_party_identifiers_party
        FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, party_id) REFERENCES public.parties (tenant_id, id)
        ON UPDATE NO ACTION ON DELETE RESTRICT,
    CONSTRAINT fk_party_identifiers_scheme
        FOREIGN KEY (identifier_scheme_id) REFERENCES public.identifier_schemes (id)
        ON UPDATE NO ACTION ON DELETE RESTRICT
);

CREATE INDEX ix_party_identifiers_party_scheme_status
    ON public.party_identifiers (tenant_id, party_id, identifier_scheme_id, status);
CREATE INDEX ix_party_identifiers_primary
    ON public.party_identifiers (tenant_id, party_id, is_primary);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_party_identifiers_verified_primary_scheme
    ON public.party_identifiers (tenant_id, party_id, identifier_scheme_id)
    WHERE is_primary = true AND status = 'VERIFIED';

COMMENT ON TABLE public.party_identifiers IS
    'Official Party identifiers. Complete values are authenticated-encrypted; exact lookup and permanent tenant-and-scheme uniqueness use the uppercase tenant-isolated HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.issuer_code IS
    'Issuing authority, for example SRI or REGISTRO_CIVIL.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.encrypted_value IS
    'Authenticated encryption; never plain text.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.encryption_key_version IS
    'Version of the runtime-injected encryption key used for this ciphertext.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.normalized_value_hash IS
    'Tenant-isolated HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint encoded as exactly 64 uppercase hexadecimal characters; used for exact lookup and permanent uniqueness within the tenant and Identifier Scheme.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.masked_value IS
    'Safe representation for UI and logs.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.is_primary IS
    'Primary identifier within the same Party and Identifier Scheme.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN public.party_identifiers.version IS
    'Optimistic concurrency version of the Party Identifier aggregate.';

CREATE TABLE public.party_outbox_events (
    id uuid DEFAULT uuidv7() NOT NULL,
    tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
    aggregate_type public.party_outbox_aggregate_type NOT NULL,
    aggregate_id uuid NOT NULL,
    aggregate_version bigint NOT NULL,
    event_type varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    event_schema_version smallint DEFAULT 1 NOT NULL,
    payload jsonb NOT NULL,
    occurred_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    correlation_id varchar(128),
    causation_id varchar(128),
    status public.outbox_status DEFAULT 'PENDING' NOT NULL,
    publish_attempts integer DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL,
    next_attempt_at timestamptz,
    last_attempt_at timestamptz,
    published_at timestamptz,
    last_error_code varchar(64),
    last_error_detail varchar(1000),
    created_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    created_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    updated_at timestamptz DEFAULT now() NOT NULL,
    updated_by varchar(128) NOT NULL,
    version bigint DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_party_outbox_events PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_outbox_nonnegative_aggregate_version CHECK (aggregate_version >= 0),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_outbox_positive_schema_version CHECK (event_schema_version > 0),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_outbox_nonnegative_attempts CHECK (publish_attempts >= 0),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_outbox_nonnegative_version CHECK (version >= 0),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_outbox_published_at
        CHECK ((status = 'PUBLISHED' AND published_at IS NOT NULL)
               OR (status <> 'PUBLISHED' AND published_at IS NULL)),
    CONSTRAINT ck_party_outbox_failed_error
        CHECK ((status = 'FAILED' AND last_error_code IS NOT NULL) OR status <> 'FAILED')
);

CREATE INDEX ix_party_outbox_delivery
    ON public.party_outbox_events (status, next_attempt_at, created_at);
CREATE INDEX ix_party_outbox_aggregate
    ON public.party_outbox_events

CREATE FUNCTION public.fn_enforce_party_detail_type()
RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $function$
DECLARE
    affected_party_id uuid;
    affected_party_ids uuid[];
    party_kind public.party_type;
    natural_detail_count integer;
    legal_detail_count integer;
BEGIN
    IF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'parties' THEN
        affected_party_ids := ARRAY[NEW.id];
    ELSIF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
        affected_party_ids := ARRAY[OLD.party_id];
    ELSIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.party_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.party_id THEN
        affected_party_ids := ARRAY[OLD.party_id, NEW.party_id];
    ELSE
        affected_party_ids := ARRAY[NEW.party_id];
    END IF;

    FOREACH affected_party_id IN ARRAY affected_party_ids
    LOOP
        SELECT p.type
          INTO party_kind
          FROM public.parties AS p
         WHERE p.id = affected_party_id;

        IF NOT FOUND THEN
            CONTINUE;
        END IF;

        SELECT count(*)
          INTO natural_detail_count
          FROM public.natural_person_details AS npd
         WHERE npd.party_id = affected_party_id;

        SELECT count(*)
          INTO legal_detail_count
          FROM public.legal_entity_details AS led
         WHERE led.party_id = affected_party_id;

        IF (party_kind = 'NATURAL_PERSON'
            AND (natural_detail_count <> 1 OR legal_detail_count <> 0))
           OR (party_kind = 'LEGAL_ENTITY'
               AND (natural_detail_count <> 0 OR legal_detail_count <> 1)) THEN
            RAISE EXCEPTION USING
                ERRCODE = 'integrity_constraint_violation',
                MESSAGE = 'party detail type invariant violated',
                DETAIL = format('party_id=%s', affected_party_id),
                CONSTRAINT = 'ct_parties_detail_type';
        END IF;
    END LOOP;

    RETURN NULL;
END;
$function$;

COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.fn_enforce_party_detail_type() IS
    'Deferred commit-time enforcement that every Party has exactly one detail row matching its immutable Party type.';

CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ct_parties_detail_type
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF type ON public.parties
DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
FOR EACH ROW
EXECUTE FUNCTION public.fn_enforce_party_detail_type();

CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ct_natural_person_details_party_type
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF party_id OR DELETE ON public.natural_person_details
DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
FOR EACH ROW
EXECUTE FUNCTION public.fn_enforce_party_detail_type();

CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ct_legal_entity_details_party_type
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF party_id OR DELETE ON public.legal_entity_details
DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
FOR EACH ROW
EXECUTE FUNCTION public.fn_enforce_party_detail_type();

-- PUBLIC receives no object access. PostgreSQL grants EXECUTE on new functions
-- to PUBLIC by default, so remove that implicit grant explicitly.
REVOKE ALL ON TABLE
    public.parties,
    public.natural_person_details,
    public.legal_entity_details,
    public.party_nationalities,
    public.identifier_schemes,
    public.party_identifiers,
    public.party_outbox_events
FROM PUBLIC;
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.fn_enforce_party_detail_type() FROM PUBLIC;

-- The runtime can perform only logical lifecycle changes; no table DELETE is
-- granted. Identifier Schemes are query-only for the runtime by Amendment 002.
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON TABLE
    public.parties,
    public.natural_person_details,
    public.legal_entity_details,
    public.party_nationalities,
    public.party_identifiers,
    public.party_outbox_events
TO party_registry_runtime;
GRANT SELECT ON TABLE public.identifier_schemes TO party_registry_runtime;

### AC-075 replacement

GIVEN two concurrent requests attempt to create the same Tenant A + Scheme S + normalized identifier N, WHEN both transactions complete, THEN the PostgreSQL uniqueness constraint permits at most one Party Identifier row to commit for that key.

### AC-076 replacement

GIVEN the normalized identifier N exists for Tenant A and Scheme S, WHEN N is submitted under Tenant B or under a different Identifier Scheme, THEN this permanent-uniqueness rule alone does not reject it; all other scheme, tenant, validation, and business rules still apply.

The authoritative DBML MUST enforce an unconditional unique constraint/index on:

`(tenant_id, identifier_scheme_id, normalized_value_hash)`

The previous partial uniqueness limited to `PENDING_VERIFICATION` and `VERIFIED` is superseded. No idempotency table or other persistence structure is authorized.
